title: JSON artifacts: the workpiece
summary: Read a Showmob artifact as a machinist reads a print: envelope, blocks, identity and lifecycle.

blocks.title: A JSON artifact is a labeled, inspectable workpiece
blocks.body: JSON is a plain text format for named values, lists and nested objects. In Showmob, one artifact object carries page identity and an ordered blocks array. It contains content and configuration, not executable page code.

blocks.heading: 1. Read the envelope
rows: Places this artifact inside a course.
The ordered content units rendered on the page.

blocks.heading: 3. What the validator checks
items: The envelope has schemaVersion 1, a valid slug, supported status and one of five themes.
The blocks array is nonempty and every block ID is stable, nonempty and unique inside the artifact.
Each block type is known and supplies the fields its renderer reads.
Registered repository artifacts also need unique slugs and explicit imports in App.tsx.

blocks.heading: 4. Check the contract
blocks.prompt: What happens if JSON names a block type the schema does not support?
options: The browser guesses the closest widget
blocks.explanation: Unknown block types are rejected before they can reach the renderer.
